newsitem.title: ITALY: Veltroni optimistic on Italy welfare talks.
newsitem.headline: Veltroni optimistic on Italy welfare talks.

text.p: Italian deputy prime minister Walter Veltroni said on Thursday that he was optimistic about talks between the government, union leaders and employers on much-needed reforms to the welfare state.

The talks began on Wednesday and immediately ran into trouble. Newspapers on Thursday carried front page headlines declaring that there had been an immediate clash with unions rejecting a document presented as a basis for talks.
"There is a government that has presented issues and there is a union that justifiably wants to put forward its own."
"The discussion will be intense and will last the time necessary to make a useful agreement."
Veltroni said all those involved wanted to carry out socially fair reforms and advised against judging the talks on a day to day basis.
Italy's hard-left Communist Refoundation leader Fausto Bertinotti said on Wednesday that the government document represented a "false start".
"What should be in it is not," Bertinotti added after inspecting the document.
Union leaders also criticised the document, with Sergio Cofferati of the CGIL trades union saying it contained "incomprehensible gaps".
Sergio D'Antoni, secretary general of the Csil trades union, told state Rai radio that the document was "unfair and wrong" and needed to be "thoroughly changed."

Italy is under pressure to carry out a convincing reform of social spending -- and to shake up its pensions system -- to prove that public finances will be kept under control before the planned 1999 launch of the single European currency.
